232335 MYNNYM

BAHAMAS PUBLIC FORECAST

BAHAMAS PUBLIC FORECAST FOR TONIGHT AND THE NEXT SIX (6) DAYS, ISSUED
BY THE BAHAMAS DEPARTMENT OF METEOROLOGY AT 6:00 P.M. EDT, Friday,
October 23, 2026. THE NEXT SCHEDULED FORECAST WILL BE ISSUED AT 6:00
A.M. EDT TOMORROW.

WARNING IN EFFECT: A Severe Weather Watch is now in effect for the
Southeast Bahamas, as well as the Turks and Caicos Islands. Please
see our latest Special Weather Statement regarding strong winds and
dangerous seas affecting the Bahamas beginning on Saturday.

GENERAL SITUATION: A deep mid- to upper-level trough over the
Caribbean Sea will continue to transport abundant tropical moisture
across the southern half of the country tonight through much of the
weekend. The trough will provide the upper-level support for
widespread cloudiness, periods of rain and showers, and isolated
thunderstorms as it interacts with a broad, meandering surface low
just east of the archipelago. This unsettled weather pattern could
produce episodes of severe weather and heavy rainfall across portions
of the Southeast Bahamas and the Turks and Caicos Islands, with
activity spreading into the Central Bahamas later tonight and
continuing through Saturday.

Outlook: Cloudy conditions and increased shower activity will
gradually spread across the Northwest Bahamas on Saturday as the
upper-level trough introduces additional moisture into the area.
Meanwhile, another surface low is expected to develop and meander
near the Central Bahamas over the weekend, resulting in periods of
unsettled weather. High pressure will strengthen across the New
England states, tightening the pressure gradient between Florida and
the Northern Bahamas. Consequently, winds will strengthen across the
Northern Bahamas and portions of the Northwest Bahamas beginning
early Sunday, potentially reaching near-gale to gale force. These
conditions could pose a serious, potentially life-threatening threat
to boaters and beachgoers. As the low-pressure system moves
northeastward into the open Atlantic, large swells are expected to
spread across the remaining islands next week, resulting in continued
hazardous marine conditions.

SPECIAL WEATHER NOTES: Rip Currents: There is a high risk of
dangerous, life-threatening rip currents across ALL Atlantic waters
of the island chain. Beachgoers, particularly those in the Northern
and Northwest Bahamas, should refrain from entering the waters
tonight through tomorrow.

Flooding: There is a high risk of flooding across the Southeast
Bahamas during heavy or prolonged rainfall periods especially in low
lying, flood prone and areas already inundated with water. There is a
slight to moderate risk of flooding across portions of the Central
Bahamas overnight and continuing through Saturday.

Severe Thunderstorm Risk: There is a slight to moderate risk of a few
isolated strong to severe thunderstorms over portions of the Central
Bahamas overnight through Saturday. These storms may produce frequent
lightning, gusty winds, heavy downpours and waterspouts. Therefore,
the public is urged to remain updated on all severe weather warnings
issued by the Bahamas Department of Meteorology.

NORTHERN BAHAMAS
(INCLUDING GRAND BAHAMA, ABACO, BIMINI & ADJACENT WATERS):
SKY CONDITIONS: Mainly fair tonight with a mix of sun and clouds
expected tomorrow.
PRECIPITATION: 10 to 30% chance of showers or thunderstorms.
WINDS: Northeasterly at 15 to 20 knots.
TEMPERATURES: MAXIMUM: MINIMUM: HEAT INDEX:
82ºF – 86ºF / 28ºC – 30ºC 70ºF – 73ºF / 21ºC – 23ºC
N/A

NORTHWEST BAHAMAS
(INCLUDING NEW PROVIDENCE, ANDROS, THE BERRY ISLANDS, ELEUTHERA &
ADJACENT WATERS):
SKY CONDITIONS: Partly cloudy tonight becoming increasingly cloudy
overnight through tomorrow.
PRECIPITATION: 20 - 30% chance of isolated showers with possible
thunderstorms tonight, increasing to a 30 - 40% chance of showers
with thunderstorms on Saturday.
WINDS: Northeasterly at 10 to 15 knots with slightly higher gusts
tonight, increasing to 15 to 20 knots tomorrow.
TEMPERATURES: MAXIMUM: MINIMUM: HEAT INDEX:
82ºF – 88ºF / 28ºC – 31ºC 73ºF – 79ºF / 23ºC – 26ºC
N/A

CENTRAL BAHAMAS
(INCLUDING EXUMA, CAT ISLAND, LONG ISLAND, SAN SALVADOR, RUM CAY &
ADJACENT WATERS):
SKY CONDITIONS: Cloudy to overcast.
PRECIPITATION: 30 - 40% chance of showers with thunderstorms tonight,
increasing to a 40 – 60% chance of scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms overnight through Saturday. Some showers may become
heavy and thunderstorms strong to severe at times.
WINDS: Northeast to east at 10 knots or less, falling light and
variable at times.
TEMPERATURES: MAXIMUM: MINIMUM: HEAT INDEX:
82ºF – 88ºF / 28ºC – 31ºC 75ºF – 79ºF / 24ºC – 26ºC
N/A

SKY CONDITIONS: Cloudy to overcast.

WINDS: East to southeast at 10 to 15 knots, falling light and

TROPICAL WEATHER OUTLOOK: Tropical cyclone formation is not expected
during the next seven days.
